title: Water-heater operating-point bias
physicalPurpose: Hold the nominal outlet temperature with the heater power required to balance steady heat loss.
principalTechnique: Operating-point bias and deviation-variable P control
objective: Measure the nominal holding output, use it as controller bias, compare the same proportional controller under a changed load, and explain why fixed bias still leaves offset.

simplifications: The recirculating volume is one well-mixed thermal state.
The cold-water load changes the zero-power equilibrium by 3 degC without changing the nominal bias.
The lesson measures nominal holding power with bounded manual trials instead of reading the plant-model parameter.
A physical holding-output measurement would include sensor, load and actuator uncertainty that this deterministic simulation omits.

baseline.limitation: Lesson 4 selected proportional gain 8 percent per degree Celsius, but the zero-bias controller retained 6.9 degrees Celsius changed-load mean absolute error.

change.decision: Measure the nominal holding output with bounded manual trials, add only that measured bias, and repeat the identical proportional-controller experiment.

disturbances: Cold-water flow increases at 60 s and shifts the zero-power equilibrium from 20 to 17 degC

acceptance.window: mean 110.1 to 120.0 s minus mean 50.1 to 60.0 s

abortPredicates: PV or MV leaves its hard limit
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The configured holding power and load event are simulation evidence, not physical heater commissioning values.

video.viewerOutcome: Measure nominal holding power with bounded manual trials, apply it as controller bias, and explain why a changed load still creates proportional-control offset.

learning.context: The recirculating water heater needs nonzero power to replace nominal heat loss while holding the desired outlet temperature, and its one-sided heater can apply only 0 to 100 percent power.
learning.reason: Lesson 4 selected gain 8 percent per degree Celsius but retained 6.9 degrees Celsius changed-load mean absolute error because zero error requested zero holding power.
theory: An operating point is a condition where outlet temperature and heater output remain steady because heat entering the water balances heat leaving it.
The required steady heater output (MV_required) is the percent heater power that balances normal heat loss at the desired operating point.
The controller bias (u0) is the measured holding output stored in the controller; it is not integral action and cannot change itself when the load changes.
The setpoint (SP) is the desired outlet-water temperature and the process value (PV) is the measured outlet-water temperature; both are measured in degrees Celsius.
The error (e) is the setpoint minus the process value, so a positive error means the measured water is too cold.
The proportional gain (Kp) states how much heater output is requested for each degree Celsius of error; Lesson 5 retains 8 percent per degree Celsius.
The temperature deviation is the current temperature minus the operating-point temperature and is measured in degrees Celsius.
The requested manipulated variable (MV_requested) is the controller calculation before limits, while the applied manipulated variable (MV_applied) is the 0 to 100 percent power the heater receives.
After all quantities are defined, the positional law is MV_requested = u0 + Kp times e, followed by MV_applied = clamp(MV_requested, 0 percent, 100 percent).
learning.workedPrediction: If a manual trial holds 35 degrees Celsius, use its measured output as bias. At SP 35 degrees Celsius and PV 35 degrees Celsius, error is zero and the Kp 8 proportional correction is zero, so a measured 75 percent bias predicts 75 percent requested and applied heater output. Predict only the direction of the changed-load error.
practicalPreparation: Start disabled and compare bounded 70, 75 and 80 percent manual trials from the same initial state, qualifying each 50.1 to 60.0 second window before selection.
Retain gain 8, use explicit Auto enable, restart after each initialization-only bias change, preserve plant, seed, load event, limits, duration and sample time, then restore Manual with zero output.
learning.baseline: Measure nominal holding output in Manual, then run the selected Lesson 4 proportional gain 8 with zero bias under the 60-second cold-water event.
learning.change: Apply only the measured 75 percent bias, restore and restart, enable Auto explicitly, and repeat the equivalent gain-8 controller run.
learning.comparison: Before results, define settling, final-window mean absolute temperature error, requested- and applied-output ranges, saturation eligibility and applied-output increase; then compare the manual candidates and the two equivalent controller runs.
learning.validation: Select 75 percent from valid manual trials, verify nominal biased error no greater than 0.1 degrees Celsius, finite bounded applied output and positive load-response direction, while retaining the 1.15 degrees Celsius changed-load error as a limitation rather than a physical acceptance claim.
learning.explanation: Explain from heat balance and the positional law why measured bias supplies nominal loss at zero error but a changed required holding output still needs proportional error.
learning.transfer: Measure operating-point bias for another self-regulating process with settled manual trials, state the actuator and operating-region assumptions, and recognize persistent changed-load error as the reason for integral action.
